group.name: Two other mods are needed, and neither is installed for you

plugin.name: MelonLoader (required) and SteamNetworkLib (multiplayer)
plugin.description:
1. MELONLOADER - required, and it is not on Nexus.
https://github.com/LavaGang/MelonLoader/releases
This mod runs on MelonLoader and cannot be installed for you. Without it the game starts completely normally and nothing tells you the mod is missing. Install it against the same copy of Schedule I you are installing this mod into, and run the game once so it creates its folders.
2. STEAMNETWORKLIB by ifBars - required for multiplayer time sync.
https://www.nexusmods.com/schedule1/mods/1396
This is what carries the clock between players. IMPORTANT: it comes in Mono and IL2CPP flavours too, and yours has to match whichever build you pick on the next page.
Skipping it is not fatal - the mod loads and single-player is completely unaffected. What you lose is time syncing between players, and nothing on screen tells you that is why; the clocks simply drift apart.
You can finish this installer first - order does not matter, only that both are present before you play.
MULTIPLAYER: time is synchronised from the host. The host's day speed is pushed to everyone in the lobby, so a client's own multiplier setting is overridden while they are connected and restored when they leave.
The config file appears after the first run, at:
UserData\DropDaDeuce-TimeNeverStops\TimeNeverStops.cfg
You can edit it while the game is running - changes are picked up within about a second.

installStep.name: Which build of Schedule I do you have?

group.name: Pick one - installing the wrong build does nothing at all

plugin.name: IL2CPP build (the normal Steam version)
plugin.description:
Installs TimeNeverStops_IL2Cpp.dll.
HOW TO TELL: open your Schedule I folder. If there is a GameAssembly.dll sitting next to Schedule I.exe, this is the one you want.
This is what a standard Steam install of Schedule I is. Pick this if you are not sure.
If you are using SteamNetworkLib for multiplayer sync, take its IL2CPP flavour to match.

plugin.name: Mono build (the alternate / beta branch)
plugin.description:
Installs TimeNeverStops_Mono.dll.
HOW TO TELL: there is NO GameAssembly.dll, and instead Schedule I_Data\Managed\ is full of .dll files (Assembly-CSharp.dll and a few hundred others).
This is the alternate build, usually opted into through Steam's beta branches.
If you are using SteamNetworkLib for multiplayer sync, take its Mono flavour to match.
